To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gene expression profiles of rat livers treated with 15 different hepatotoxins correlated well with the histopathological and clinical chemistry effects of the agents.
gene expression profiles can predict the mechanism of toxicity of a compound and can be used to cluster hepatotoxins according to mechanism.
we have identified a number of gene expression profiles that can be used to predict the mechanism of toxicity for a variety of hepatotoxants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of microarray analysis and the development of gene expression signatures to the field of hepatotoxicology.
the use of DNA microarrays to identify gene expression signatures associated with the toxicity of various drugs and chemicals.
the use of microarray technology to identify genes whose expression is altered by a wide variety of toxic agents, including drugs, environmental toxins, and carcinogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gene expression profiling can provide a powerful tool for the classification of toxicants and the elucidation of the mechanisms of action of toxicants.
gene expression profiles can be clustered based upon the mechanism of toxicity and that this clustering is highly reproducible.
microarray analysis is a powerful tool for toxicology and that it can be used to predict toxicity, classify toxins, and identify potential biomarkers of toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gene expression profiles of the liver can be used as a biomarker for hepatotoxicity.
microarrays can be used to classify hepatotoxins into groups based on the mechanism of toxicity.
microarray technology can provide valuable information for safety assessment of drugs and environmental toxins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gene expression profiles can provide an early warning of the mechanism of action of a hepatotoxic agent.
gene expression profiles can be used to classify hepatotoxins into clusters based on the mechanism of injury.
microarray analysis can be a powerful tool to identify gene expression signatures that are associated with the mechanism of action of a compound.
